column3: The Hebrew calls them sons of the exile; BSB says exiles.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes weakening the hands of Judah’s people; BSB says discouraging them.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses active unnamed plural subjects writing an accusation; BSB uses the passive “an accusation was lodged.”
The Hebrew repeats Aramaic for both the writing and its rendering; BSB names Aramaic only for the writing and adds “then.”
The Aramaic says “one letter”; BSB says “the letter.”
The Aramaic lists the Susa people, Dahites, and Elamites separately; BSB combines the final groups as Elamites of Susa. Earlier group names are rendered as judges and officials in BSB.
The Aramaic says the city of Samaria, singular; BSB says cities of Samaria. It names Beyond the River; BSB specifies west of the Euphrates.
The Aramaic says Beyond the River; BSB specifies west of the Euphrates.
The Aramaic describes the walls as completed; BSB describes their restoration as ongoing.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Aramaic says “we salt the salt of the palace” and speaks of seeing the king’s nakedness; BSB says being in palace service and allowing dishonor.
The Aramaic repeats “the book of records”; BSB uses “these books” for the second reference.
The Aramaic says “a portion in Beyond the River”; BSB says dominion west of the Euphrates.
The Aramaic says “their associates”; BSB addresses “your associates.” It names Beyond the River; BSB specifies west of the Euphrates.
The Aramaic describes the letter as read distinctly before him; BSB makes translating and reading separate actions.
The Aramaic uses unnamed active plural subjects for searching and finding; BSB uses passive clauses.
The Aramaic names Beyond the River; BSB specifies the region west of the Euphrates.
The Aramaic says until a decree is issued by him, using the passive; BSB says “until I so order.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Aramaic says they stopped them “by arm and force”; BSB says “forcibly.”
Close to the Hebrew.
